summary: A compact progress rail that expands into a section list. A disclosure, not a menu — and it computes nothing itself.
useWhen: a long document or page needs an in-page section index with reading progress
the caller already knows the scroll fraction and the active section

useInstead.when: the sections are peer views rather than positions in one document
it is site navigation rather than in-page position

a11y.role: disclosure — a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls
guarantees: the rail is reachable by Tab and opens with Enter or Space, not just hover
closes on outside pointerdown and on Escape
requires: `progress` as 0–100 and `activeId` — the component has no opinion on where they come from
handling `onSelect` yourself: it reports the choice and does not scroll anywhere
notes: Deliberately not `role="menu"` — see the stylesheet header. It is a disclosure with a list inside it, not a menu with roving focus.
Not a focus trap: it is the minimum a disclosure needs to not trap the page once opened.

antiPatterns.dont: expecting it to scroll the page when a section is chosen
antiPatterns.why: it reports the choice, matching Menu — what "select this section" means is the page's decision

antiPatterns.dont: deriving `progress` from a scroll listener without throttling
antiPatterns.why: this re-renders the rail on every scroll frame

antiPatterns.dont: expecting every section to be visible at once
antiPatterns.why: the panel caps at 60vh and scrolls — a document-length index would otherwise grow off both edges of the viewport, taking the rows nearest the active one with it
